goal: Find reliability defects in the Bakeoff multi-lens and parallel-flow code paths across the named target files.
background: Branch: main, HEAD: d7cc4a4 (runtime visibility); local uncommitted changes exist in internal/runner/runner.go and others; review the current working tree.
Review target files (all 7, no other files):
- skills/bakeoff-run/SKILL.md (411 lines) - drafting and multi-lens contract for /bakeoff:run
- commands/run.md (15 lines) - slash command entry point
- references/run-appendix.md (205 lines) - split and multi-lens preview templates and presets
- internal/commands/researchcmd/run.go (1031 lines) - research command implementation including multi-lens fanout
- internal/runner/runner.go (1106 lines) - provider runner and concurrency layer
Scope: multi-lens and parallel-flow code paths and their interactions across these 7 files.
Lens: RELIABILITY only. Correctness and maintainability are covered by sibling lens runs.
Acceptance for findings: every finding must cite file:line, name a concrete failure mode (cancellation, timeout, crash, partial failure, resource exhaustion), and explain the observable consequence.

facet.focus: Context and cancellation propagation, timeout handling, partial-failure recovery, goroutine and file-descriptor leaks, ledger atomicity and crash safety, parallel child lifecycle, and exit-code semantics for partial-failure scenarios.
include: context cancellation that does not propagate to in-flight provider or child work
timeout, retry, backoff, or heartbeat logic with a concrete failure mode
goroutine leaks, file-descriptor leaks, or unbounded resource use
ledger writes that are not atomic, idempotent, or crash-safe (partial writes, lost updates, missing fsync where required)
parallel child lifecycle: orphan or zombie handling, pid/exit/stdout/stderr file race conditions, missing reaps
incorrect exit code mapping for partial-failure scenarios (multi-lens, split, judge fail, decision-incomplete)
triage state machine transitions that lose work on retry, interruption, or stale-state restart
exclude: issues outside the 7 named target files
correctness bugs unrelated to a failure mode (covered by the correctness lens)
naming, layering, or duplication concerns (covered by the maintainability lens)
broad rewrite proposals unrelated to a specific failure mode
